sources.title: Chamber of Commerce of the State of New York, Rapid Transit in New York City and in the Other Great Cities (1906), ch. 4 "Bridges to Brooklyn"

towerHeightM.note: height (P2048): tower top above the water. The 1906 text gives 272 ft (82.9 m).

totalLengthM.note: length (P2043) 5,989 ft. The game fits the bridge to its LION frame (spanM), so the approaches are shorter.

midspanClearanceM.note: vertical clearance (P2793): the deck top at mid-span

roadwayAtTowersM.note: "at the towers the height of the roadway is 119.25 feet"

towerAtCornice.note: 126 by 43 ft at the base of the cornice

archSpanM.note: the three columns above the roadway are united by arches of 33.75 ft span

archRadiusM.note: each arch is two arcs of 48 1/6 ft radius (a pointed arch)

archApexAboveRoadwayM.note: 117 ft, a commonly quoted figure not found in the public-domain text read; sets where the arches spring

corniceBaseM.note: height of the cornice base above the water, proportioned from the tower top and arch apex

promenadeAboveDeckM.note: the promenade is 12 ft above the floor beams

outerRoadwayWidthM.note: outside roadways 18.75 ft wide in the clear

sideSpanM.note: (total length - both approaches - main span) / 2, from the values above

anchorage.note: stylised anchorage blocks sized to take the cables; mostly hidden under the game's land top

readabilityScale.note: Thin members are drawn this many times their true width so they read at game distance; suspenders and stays are also grouped (drawn sparser than the real 1,520).

gameScale.note: Game scale (orchestrator decision 2026-10-08, the user may overrule): heights x1.8 and widths x2 against the real numbers above, so the towers, deck and cables read at the 3,000-4,500 m game camera. Lengths along the axis stay real (the towers 486 m apart, fitted to the LION frame).
